about: Accounts, sessions, devices and rate limits for protocol v2 (docs/ACCOUNTS.md › HTTP protocol). Owner: the Worker
builder; frozen by step 1. Runners: cloud/test/auth.test.ts (the Worker, through handle(request, env, now)) and
crates/kanso-sync/tests/conformance.rs (MemoryServer, through kanso_sync::Api).
Each case starts from an empty server: the settings 0002_accounts.sql seeds, except signup = "open"; no accounts;
the clock at `start` (a UTC midnight, Unix ms); one client IP (Worker: no CF-Connecting-IP, so "unknown", and no
AUTH_LIMITER binding). Values: any JSON string exactly "$name" stands for values[name] (any JSON value) or for the
value last captured under that name.
Steps, exactly one kind each; `note` is for readers and ignored:
{settings: {name: value}} sets settings rows (D1 UPDATE; MemoryServer::set_setting).
{admin: "disable" | "enable", username} and {admin: "quota", username, quota: {docs?, doc_bytes?, files?,
file_bytes?}} (a number, or null for the default) act as the admin script does.
{request: <route>, t?, as?, token?, body?, query?, path?, file?, status, response?, capture?} sends one request.
route: a kanso_sync::Route name (health, prelogin, signup, login, recover_start, recover_finish, logout, account,
password, recovery_key, delete, set_device, devices, revoke_device, push, changes, put_file, get_file).
t: ms since start, never decreasing; default the previous step's. as: the captured token to send as
Authorization: Bearer; token: a literal token; neither: no header (the typed client sends an empty token, which
is malformed the same way). body: the JSON body. query: {since?, limit?} for changes (numbers). path:
{device_id} or {wire_id}. file: the PUT body as base64url; x-kanso-sha256 is its SHA-256. status: the HTTP
status. response: a pattern for the JSON body; get_file's body is matched as {bytes: base64url}. capture:
{name: dotted path into the response}.
{raw: {method, path, headers?, body?}, as?, t?, status, response?, response_headers?, runner: "worker"} sends
input no typed client can produce. "$name" inside path is replaced; a body that is exactly "$name" is sent as
that value's base64url-decoded bytes, any other body as its UTF-8 text.
runner: "worker" on a step or a case: only the Worker runs it; MemoryServer skips it. No such step changes
state, except rate-limit counts that later steps in its case don't depend on.
Patterns: objects match key by key (other keys are ignored, and null also matches a missing key); arrays match
element by element and must have the same length; "*" matches any non-null value; "$name" must equal that value;
"!$name" must differ from it; anything else must be equal. An error body's message is never compared.
Expected values were cross-checked against an independent model of the spec before freezing.
